pages.headline: Higher inflation raises the bar for market conviction
pages.lead: October consumer inflation and the RBI's policy tightening require investors to separate headline price moves from verified earnings and cash flows.
analysis: An interest-rate increase changes the discount-rate backdrop; sector conclusions still need dated valuations and company disclosures.
The October CPI release is provisional. Any claimed market reaction must be backed by actual NSE close-to-close data.
pages.risk_note: Do not interpret this macro summary as a market direction forecast or portfolio instruction.

pages.headline: Growth and inflation must be read together
pages.lead: MoSPI reported October CPI inflation of 6.09% and September industrial-production growth of 6.7%; the periods are different and must not be mixed.
analysis: October food-price inflation was 8.94%, raising household cost pressure; consumer-company margins need issuer-level checks.
The RBI raised the policy repo rate to 5.50% in October; review borrowing costs alongside demand and industrial output.
pages.risk_note: These figures are from separately dated releases, not a same-period composite indicator.

pages.headline: Nifty 50: validate the price series before charting
pages.lead: The NSE supplies a dated 30 October snapshot, but one observation does not support a trendline, momentum score or monthly technical forecast.
analysis: Build the chart only from matched trading-date closes with audited units, adjustment rules and no missing sessions.
Separate market breadth from index-weighted price action; the leading constituents can move the benchmark without broad participation.
pages.risk_note: Support and resistance, RSI and trend conclusions are withheld until a complete verified time series is available.

pages.headline: Bank Nifty and major indices require comparable dates
pages.lead: An index comparison is meaningful only when every benchmark has the same valuation date, observation frequency and return calculation.
analysis: Use official close-to-close series for Nifty 50, Nifty Bank, Midcap 150 and Smallcap 250 rather than mixing live and EOD values.
Show both percentage change and absolute index levels with correct units; a point difference is not comparable across indices.
pages.risk_note: No relative-performance ranking is approved without all official matched-date observations.

pages.headline: Institutional flows need instrument-specific context
pages.lead: Foreign and domestic investor flow totals must be sourced by segment and settlement date; cash trades and derivatives cannot be summed as one signal.
analysis: Compare verified cash-market FII and DII figures with turnover and price reaction for the same session.
Describe breadth using reproducible advancing, declining and unchanged constituent counts, not market anecdotes.
pages.risk_note: FII/DII totals and market-breadth claims remain withheld until official dated tables are captured.

pages.headline: Sector rotation: distinguish returns from narratives
pages.lead: Sector leadership requires a consistent index universe and matched start and end dates; a high daily move is not monthly leadership.
analysis: Use total-return and price-return conventions explicitly, with comparability checks before sorting sector rankings.
Concentration, earnings cycles and policy sensitivity deserve separate commentary after source confirmation.
pages.risk_note: Sector performance winners, laggards and percentages are not stated without official matching series.

pages.headline: Large-cap research starts with issuer evidence
pages.lead: Large-cap company pages should connect audited operating results, balance sheets and cash generation to valuation, not only index weight.
analysis: Use the issuer's own latest filed consolidated results before secondary estimates or headline news.
Compare operating margin, cash conversion and leverage only after units and accounting periods align.
pages.risk_note: No company-specific results or recommendations are certified in this draft pending issuer-filing review.

pages.headline: Mid-cap research demands stronger liquidity checks
pages.lead: Mid-cap company research should test earnings quality, working-capital cycles and liquidity rather than extrapolating past share-price returns.
analysis: Confirm the current Midcap 150 universe and free-float liquidity using dated NSE information.
Separate unusually strong quarterly profit from recurring operating cash flow and sustainable margins.
pages.risk_note: Individual mid-cap company conclusions are withheld until dated issuer financials and price records are reconciled.

pages.headline: Small-cap analysis must price in execution risk
pages.lead: Small-cap research requires explicit trading-liquidity and balance-sheet checks because unstable pricing can magnify sizing mistakes.
analysis: Validate the Smallcap 250 universe and identify low-volume names before any peer or valuation comparison.
Reject comparisons across different fiscal periods, standalone versus consolidated accounts and inconsistent sector groupings.
pages.risk_note: No qualifying small-cap stock list is established by these broad-market data sources alone.

pages.headline: Fundamentals: reconcile statements before valuation
pages.lead: An issuer research spotlight needs filing dates, auditor scope, income-statement units, cash flow and share-count consistency.
analysis: Treat exceptional gains and accounting reclassifications separately from recurring operating earnings.
Cross-check debt, related-party notes, dilution and contingent liabilities before any comparative multiples.
pages.risk_note: Stock-specific valuation ratios cannot be published without original filings and a dated share-price reference.

pages.headline: Strategy Lab: test a rate-and-inflation scenario
pages.lead: Use October's RBI tightening and November's CPI release to define conditional monitoring rules, not automatic market trades.
analysis: Scenario A: inflation persists; review credit sensitivity and valuation assumptions once actual issuer figures are confirmed.
Scenario B: price pressure moderates; compare earnings revisions against the same risk controls and liquidity requirements.
pages.risk_note: These are analytical scenarios, not forecasts or personalized buy/sell instructions.

pages.headline: Upcoming data calendar and policy checkpoints
pages.lead: The next monthly research update must distinguish a scheduled release date from an already published observation.
analysis: MoSPI has scheduled the FY27 second-quarter GDP estimate for 30 November 2026; do not quote it before release.
The RBI MPC's next scheduled meeting is 2-4 December 2026; policy outcomes must remain unfilled until announced.
pages.risk_note: Future outcomes, final statistics and policy decisions are unknown as of 23 November 2026.

pages.headline: Next month: focus on evidence and risk limits
pages.lead: Policy tightening and inflation risk argue for disciplined scenario analysis rather than a single unsupported market forecast.
analysis: Review sector concentration, balance-sheet interest sensitivity and high-frequency volatility only with verified histories.
Monitor revised inflation, quarterly GDP and the next RBI resolution as distinct dated events.
pages.risk_note: Neither a target index level nor investment allocation is approved from this evidence set.

pages.headline: Research method, omissions and source discipline
pages.lead: This draft separates source-cited macro facts from unverified market prices and issuer claims; missing values are explicitly withheld.
analysis: NSE data are not authenticated merely by a matching URL; original bytes, SHA-256 and field-level reconciliation remain necessary.
Company pages require original exchange filings, calendar alignment, independent calculation checks and owner sign-off.
pages.risk_note: Not investment advice. This editorial draft is not approved for customer distribution or Telegram delivery.
